transcript: Showering in the morning is extremely dangerous and most people do it every day. When you first wake up your body isn't fully activated, your blood pressure is low, your cortisol is rising, and your internal temperature is still trying to warm up. Hitting your system with hot water at that moment forces your heart and blood vessels to work harder than they should. Your vessels suddenly widen, your heart rate jumps and for many people that leads to dizziness, nausea or that almost blackout feeling. Morning showers also remove the natural oils your skin built up overnight, right when your body is trying to restore them. That leaves your skin drier throughout the day, more sensitive to sunlight and more easily irritated. Even your hair is affected, washing it during peak cortisol hours can increase frizz, oil imbalance and scalp dryness. Night showers on the other hand do the opposite. They calm the nervous system, they lower stress hormones, they help your body release heat slowly before sleep, they wash away the dirt, sweat and tension you carried through the day, so it does not sit on your skin all night. But here is the strangest part. This isn't really about showers, it's about how most people live out of sync with their own nervous system, small daily habits done at the wrong time quietly drain the body. Healing does not require force, it requires alignment. Listen to your body before you follow routines, your system speaks softly, but it always tells the truth. If this speaks to you, my 30-day healing journey and e-books are waiting in the link on my profile.
